title: NASA Spacecraft Markings
slide_intent: Teach designers to choose identifiers according to available surface and scientific function. A small, unobstructed mark can carry more information than a crowded group.
strategic_value: NASA can identify spacecraft of different shapes while letting each scientific instrument’s operational constraints determine the marking scheme.
demonstration: Three annotated craft demonstrate distinct solutions. The telescope uses red at the scale of its smaller diameter. The Solar Maximum Mission craft pairs a gray mark with the flag and country name. The exposure facility uses a red mark alone above a panel of matching width.
practical_value: Compare the telescope, satellite and exposure facility before choosing a mark size or adding a national identifier. Use an actual structural dimension for scale.

content_islands.name: Selection principles
content_islands.spec: Place the principles and minimum marking guidance in the upper-left text area.

content_islands.name: Telescope and solar mission
content_islands.spec: Use two separate angled views with their short notes. Keep the side panels, mark, flag and type legible so the available surfaces can be compared.

content_islands.name: Exposure facility
content_islands.spec: Show the elongated faceted structure across the lower field. Keep its single red mark visible above the reference panel and explain the width relationship beside it.
